To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) AKT activity is decreased and glucose 6-phosphates and ATP levels are decreased during mitotic arrest, suggesting a metabolic vulnerability; 2) A high-content siRNAscreen to detect novel metabolic vulnerabilities in mitotically-arrested ovarian cancer cells identified PFKFB4 as a novel target; 3) PFKFB4 is necessary for cell survival in mitoticallyarrested cells, and its depletion enhances cell death after mitotic arrest.
mitotic arrest in some ovarian cancer cell lines leads to a decrease in AKT phosphorylation and glycolytic intermediates, and that PFKFB3/4 depletion sensitizes mitotic cells to cell death.
mitotically arrested cancer cells are vulnerable to metabolic inhibition and that targeting the glycolytic enzymes PFKFB3 and PFKFB4 can induce cell death in mitotic cancer cells.
